visibleAssistantStatements.text: The implementation will keep the ledger inside each adapter’s persisted state, not in upload payloads: hashed identities plus sanitized date/token tuples only. Existing 0.4.3 file contributions will be carried as an unattributed content-free baseline while old raw identity maps are converted or discarded; current scans then add only identities not already observed. I’ll preserve partial-pass retention by committing ledger changes only for fully parsed records, except identity conflicts, which produce a partial result while unrelated records continue.

The core path is now wired: event analyzers expose sanitized `(identity, tuple)` records, JSONL collectors and OpenCode commit bounded ledgers, Claude migrates its prior identity map to hashes, and connection/sync state transfers adapter state by stable local source ID when server source IDs change. I’m running the reader suite diagnostically before adding regressions to catch preserved-contract breakage introduced by the refactor.

The preservation failures are narrowed to two intentional semantic changes: a committed event now remains in the ledger after file truncation, and a replacement with a new event identity is treated as a new event. I fixed provisional-tail aggregation so uncommitted partial records are shown without being added to the ledger; next I’m adding explicit switch/conflict regressions and updating only the truncation assertion that the task deliberately replaces.

The focused regressions now cover all five JSONL event adapters, OpenCode SQLite history replacement, conflicting tuples, and conservative pre-ledger migration; Claude’s persisted identity keys are hashed as well. The implementation review also caught and fixed bounded-ledger partial signaling and a legacy Claude partial-state path that could otherwise retain raw IDs. I’m starting the final checks now: targeted new behavior first, then the three requested preservation suites in separate invocations.

All final behavior and preservation checks pass: targeted ledger/migration/conflict tests, the full reader suite, config suite, protocol suite, and Claude state-security regression. I’m doing the final diff/scope review now, then I’ll attempt the repository-mandated `corepack pnpm verify`; if the documented uncached dependency limitation blocks it, I’ll report that as unavailable rather than treating it as a pass.

The final review found one preservation edge case in OpenCode: an unsupported partial scan must retain an existing ledger’s accepted entries, while still returning the old empty result when no ledger exists. That is fixed; I’m rerunning the new OpenCode regression and all three requested suites after this last edit.
